boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Sabine Pass record (September 24-25, 1862) in Operations to Blockade the Texas Coast [September 1862-January 1863]. The Taylor's Bayou bridge raid of September 27, the capture of blockade runners and Crocker's Calcasieu and Mermentau expeditions are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field names the Kensington, Rachel Seaman and mortar schooner Henry James and gives the Fort Griffith garrison as 30 with 25 mounted men 3 1/2 miles away (CS bounds 55 and 55); the live field reads 0. Debray, at Houston on September 25, says Major Irvine had only 30 men at the fort and about 25 mounted men 3 1/2 miles off, the rest of the battalion being on yellow-fever furlough. Spaight says a detachment of Company B garrisoned the works and a detachment of 26 of Company E arrived at nightfall. Crocker names his three vessels and a strong party from the Kensington, without figures.
claims.rationale: Debray's second-hand figure, reported from Houston on September 25, matches the frozen table; Spaight's 26 arrived at nightfall on September 24, a different moment; the Union crews are not counted. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: Crocker says his vessels failed to cross the bar the first night, only the Rachel Seaman crossed next evening, and the Henry Janes was kedged over; his night boat expedition was entangled on reefs. Spaight says the battery's shot fell short while the enemy's longer-range guns reached the works.
claims.rationale: Natural bar and reefs and the guns' relative range, from interested reports; tag unresolved because gun range is not terrain.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Acting Master Frederick Crocker (navy) and Major J. S. Irvine; the live page gives Crocker as lieutenant, not adopted. Spaight says Irvine commanded at the Pass in his absence and Captain K. D. Keith commanded the battery. Crocker received the surrender of the town and credits Pennington's getting the Henry Janes over the bar with the expedition's success.
claims.rationale: Command roles from interested reports; no automatic sole credit.

open_questions: Irvine's and Keith's own reports (if any), Hooper's and Pennington's reports (ORN 19; seen only in part or as search hits), returns and maps remain deferred. Debray's report is the targeted follow-up for the frozen 30 and 25.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Spaight's September 26, 1862 report and Crocker's October 2, 1862 report (ORN) are interested accounts from opposite sides; Debray's September 25 report, written at Houston from messengers, is a separate family used as the follow-up. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.

No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Participants are named as the sources name them; characterizations in the sources (including 'hostile', 'savages', 'massacre' or 'battle') are quoted as the sources' own words and not adopted.
